battle.name: 羅馬內戰
battle.theater: 義大利半島與地中海東部
battle.brief: 凱撒前四十四年三月十五日在羅馬遇刺，安東尼、屋大維與流亡的布魯圖斯派為爭奪軍團與行省稅收開火，戰火由意大利蔓延到西西里、希臘與埃及，以亞克興海戰的勝利收場。十四年間，共和國的元老院與公民大會被打成空殼。卡面的亞述長弓代表複合弓譜系，戰中由克里特弓手與帕提亞馬上弓手使用。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 這場內戰由公元前四十四年三月凱撒遇刺引爆，到公元前三十年埃及戰事結束才收尾，交戰方大致分成四個軍事政治集團。第一是安東尼派：馬可·安東尼出身騎士家族，前四十三年出任執政官，握有羅馬城，並以凱撒老友與遺囑執行人的身份接管其政治遺產，同年十一月與雷必達、屋大維組成第二次三頭同盟，憑《提提亞法》取得五年非常統治權與沒收對頭財產的權力。第二是屋大維派：屋大維是凱撒姐姐阿提婭的兒子，前四十三年以自己名下產莊招募八個軍團，四十二年聯同安東尼在腓立比擊敗布魯圖斯，其後逐步接管高盧、西班牙與埃及運來的穀物稅源。第三是解放者派：馬可·尤尼烏斯·布魯圖斯與蓋烏斯·卡西烏斯·隆基努斯刺殺凱撒後率軍東走，在馬其頓、希臘與小亞細亞收攏散兵，聲稱要維護元老院與共和自由，卻在腓立比一役全軍覆沒。第四是西克斯都·龐培派：他手上是龐培留下的海軍殘部，控制西西里、撒丁島與地中海中部的糧食航線，前四十三年至三十六年同屋大維爭奪意大利南部，終敗於米利與瑙洛庫斯兩場海戰。外圍還有埃及托勒密王朝與帕提亞帝國：安東尼先後迎娶克利奧佩特拉七世與帕提亞王女，把內戰拉進東地中海與兩河。各集團的指揮系統都建在共和國的軍團、執政官與元老院決議之上，但真正決定戰局的，是將軍的私人聲望、隨軍錢糧與老兵軍團的忠誠度；元老院的命令在戰場上往往沒有約束力。
countriesEn: The civil war that began with the murder of Caesar in March 44 BC and only ended with the Egyptian campaign in 30 BC split into four military-political blocs. The first was Antony's: Marcus Antonius came from an equestrian family, became consul in 43 BC, held Rome, and took over Caesar's political inheritance as his friend and the executor of his will; in November of that same year he joined Lepidus and Octavian in the second triumvirate, gaining five years of extraordinary powers under the lex Titia together with the right to confiscate the property of their enemies. The second was Octavian's: Octavian, the son of Caesar's sister Atia, raised eight legions on his own estates in 43 BC, and with Antony beat Brutus at Philippi in 42 BC, after which he gradually took over the grain tax of Gaul, Spain and Egypt. The third was the Liberators: Marcus Junius Brutus and Gaius Cassius Longinus marched east after the murder, gathering the scattered legions of Macedonia, Greece and Asia Minor and claiming to defend the Senate and republican liberty, only to be wiped out at Philippi. The fourth was Sextus Pompeius: he held Pompey's remaining fleet, controlled Sicily, Sardinia and the grain routes of the central Mediterranean, and fought Octavian over southern Italy from 43 to 36 BC before being beaten at Mylae and Naulochus. Around them stood the Ptolemaic kingdom of Egypt and the Parthian empire, for Antony married first Cleopatra VII and then a Parthian princess, dragging the civil war into the eastern Mediterranean and Mesopotamia. Every command system rested on the Republic's legions, consuls and senatorial decrees, but what really decided campaigns was a general's personal prestige, the money and grain that followed the army, and the loyalty of the veteran legions; senatorial orders had little binding force on the battlefield.
people: 決定這場內戰走向的人多半死於戰場或自殺。蓋烏斯·尤利烏斯·凱撒出身拉丁顯貴家族，前五十九年首度當執政官，前四十九年取得高盧行省軍權後越過盧比孔河，前四十八年法薩盧斯之役擊敗龐培，前四十四年三月十五日在羅馬劇院被布魯圖斯等人刺殺。馬可·安東尼在凱撒葬禮上公開追悼死者，前四十三年任執政官，是三頭同盟中軍力最盛的一方，前三十七年與屋大維正式分裂，帶兵東行並在亞歷山大里亞建「安東尼亞」紀念城，前三十四年自稱神祇，與羅馬本部的聯繫日漸疏離。屋大維本名蓋烏斯·屋大維，十六歲被收為養子後憑遺囑入主，先後贏得腓立比、西西里與亞克興三場戰役。馬可·維普薩尼烏斯·阿格里帕是最關鍵的技術型將領：騎兵出身，靠米利、瑙洛庫斯與亞克興三場海戰替屋大維奪下地中海。布魯圖斯與卡西烏斯在西方的政治人望極高，東征之後卻缺乏補給與海上縱援；西克斯都·龐培的海上實力在米利、瑙洛庫斯兩戰被封鎖殲滅。埃及的克利奧佩特拉七世以資金與穀船支援安東尼，最終在羅馬海軍進入埃及後自盡。
peopleEn: Most of the men who decided the course of this civil war died in battle or by their own hand. Gaius Julius Caesar came from a distinguished Latin family, was consul for the first time in 59 BC, took command of the Gallic province and crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC, defeated Pompey at Pharsalus in 48 BC, and was stabbed in a Roman theatre on 15 March 44 BC by Brutus and the rest. Marcus Antonius publicly mourned the dead man at Caesar's funeral, became consul in 43 BC, and was the strongest of the triumvirs in armed strength; in 37 BC he split formally from Octavian, marched east, founded the city of Antonia in Alexandria, and proclaimed himself a god in 34 BC, growing steadily more distant from Rome itself. Octavian, born Gaius Octavius, entered the inheritance as Caesar's adopted son at sixteen, and won in turn at Philippi, in Sicily and at Actium. Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa was the decisive technical commander: a cavalryman by origin, he won the Mediterranean for Octavian in the sea battles of Mylae, Naulochus and Actium. Brutus and Cassius had enormous political standing in the West but after their march east lacked supply and support at sea; the naval force of Sextus Pompeius was shut in and destroyed at Mylae and Naulochus. Cleopatra VII of Egypt supported Antony with money and grain ships, and in the end took her own life when the Roman fleet entered Egypt.
kits: 卡面那件亞述長弓代表複合弓這一系的技術譜系：以木為芯、角與筋腱包覆的弓臂，配上鐵質箭鏃，拉力大而射程遠，正是亞述人「弓與鐵」兼施的底子。羅馬共和國晚期的意大利軍營裡，這類長弓並非公民兵的制式裝備，而是外籍弓手帶入的：克里特弓手用輕便的角木弓配黑尾箭，敘利亞與龐貝尼亞弓手用能發射標槍式箭的重弓，帕提亞騎兵用的角筋複合弓可以連續拋射，弓手伏在馬腹下射擊再即時轉向。凱撒整編軍團時，每個軍團除八十個步兵百人隊外，另配約一百二十名弓手與一百二十名輕裝散兵，並配三個騎兵大隊各十個中隊；羅馬主力仍靠朱庇特短劍、圓盾與重投槍，弓與砲只負責騷擾、壓制與遮蔽。真正左右這十幾年戰局的，是羅馬的攻城與航海手段：配重式投石機、手拉式弩砲、覆以藤蔓與防禦牆的攻城塔、撞槌、龜甲陣，以及用於封鎖港口的小型快艇。海戰用的五排槳戰艦配三角前帆與縱帆，舷上可裝弩砲與登船橋，抓鉤、燃火矢裝置與盛著燃燒液的小艇都見於亞克興。軍需品包括帳篷、木柵營盤、攻城用的柴捆與填壕的土方，運輸靠騾車與牛車，遠征糧食靠船隊，道路則以阿比亞道與艾格納提亞道維持。
kitsEn: The Assyrian longbow on the card stands for one technical lineage of the composite bow: a wooden core faced with horn and backed with sinew, carrying iron arrowheads, powerful and long-ranged, the very base of the Assyrian pairing of bow and iron. In the late Republican camps of Italy such a longbow was not a citizen's standard issue but arrived with foreign bowmen: Cretan archers used light horn-and-wood bows with barbed arrows, Syrian and Pontic archers used heavy bows able to throw javelin-like bolts, and Parthian mounted archers used horn-and-sinew composite bows that could loose repeatedly, shooting from under the horse's belly before turning instantly. When Caesar reorganized the legion, each legion besides its eighty centuries of infantry received roughly one hundred and twenty archers and one hundred and twenty light skirmishers, together with three cavalry units of ten turmae each; the Roman main body still fought with the short sword, the round shield and the heavy pilum, and bow and artillery did nothing but harass, pin down and cover. What really decided these fourteen years was Roman siegecraft and seamanship: torsion onagers, hand-drawn cheiroballistae, assault towers covered with vineae and plutei, battering rams, testudes, and small fast boats used to blockade harbours. The quinqueremes that fought at sea carried a lateen foresail and a square sail, with cheiroballistae and boarding bridges on deck, and grappling irons, fire-arrow gear and pots of burning liquid all appear at Actium. The baggage train included tents, palisaded camps, brushwood for sieges and earth for filling ditches; draught animals pulled carts and ox-waggons, distant campaigns were supplied by ship, and the roads were kept open by the Via Appia and the Via Egnatia.
tactics: 這場內戰的戰術可以分成三種形態。會戰靠地形決定部署：腓立比之戰，布魯圖斯佔據山脊，卡西烏斯列陣於平原低谷，屋大維把主力集中到狹窄通道，突擊卡西烏斯的一翼再回身擊潰布魯圖斯的營地；亞克興之戰，屋大維的艦隊採防禦楔形陣，裝有弩砲的輕快小艇沿正面反覆衝擊安東尼的戰線，安東尼把主力壓在右翼與中央，最終讓出缺口而全線崩解。圍城方面，屋大維圍佩魯賈時以壕溝與土壘封住城牆的射界，遠處用投石機與弓箭壓制，冬天來臨前逼守軍屈服；西西里戰線則完全靠海。海上戰術的重點是封鎖而非接舷：以小艇群封住海峽、用燒船衝擊敵縱列、切斷敵方糧船，同時保持己方補給線不斷。兵制上，各方都在徵召老兵與還鄉農民，兵員流動性高，忠誠靠軍餉與戰功維持；遠征路線上，安東尼的軍隊要從意大利南下到布蘭迪西烏姆再渡海到伊庇魯斯，渡海批次、糧草與船隻編組直接決定作戰節奏。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this civil war fall into three forms. Decisive battles were settled by terrain: at Philippi, Brutus held the ridge and Cassius deployed in the hollow of the plain, and Octavian concentrated his force in the narrow defile, struck one wing of Cassius and then turned back on Brutus's camp; at Actium, Octavian's fleet formed a defensive wedge and light boats carrying cheiroballistae battered Antony's line again and again, while Antony massed his strength on the right and in the centre, and the line finally opened and came apart. In sieges, Octavian's encirclement of Perugia sealed the range of the walls with ditches and earth banks, kept the defenders under stone-throwers and arrows from a distance, and wore them down before winter; the Sicilian theatre was decided entirely at sea. The point of naval tactics was blockade rather than boarding: sealing straits with swarms of small boats, driving fire-ships into the enemy's line, cutting off the enemy's grain ships, while keeping one's own supply line open. On recruitment, all sides called up veterans and returning farmers, so the manpower was fluid and loyalty rested on pay and plunder; on the long marches, Antony's army had to move down the Italian peninsula to Brundisium and then cross the sea to Epirus, and the size of the convoys, the grain and the grouping of the transports set the rhythm of the campaign.
data: 有根據可查的數字集中在編制與艦船兩端。共和國晚期的軍團約五千四百至六千人，編為八十個步兵百人隊；凱撒整編後每團另加約一百二十名弓手、一百二十名輕裝散兵，並附三個騎兵大隊、每大隊十個中隊、每中隊約三十騎。屋大維前四十三年以私人產莊招募八個軍團。腓立比兩戰在公元前四十二年十月相隔數日爆發，雙方各自出兵數萬，戰場縱深只有數里，十二月布魯圖斯與卡西烏斯相繼自盡。公元前三十六年的米利與瑙洛庫斯兩場海戰決定了西西里戰線；公元前三十一年九月二日亞克興海戰，安東尼一方約五百艘戰船，屋大維一方約二百六十艘，屋大維的船吃水較深、噸位較大，安東尼的船載登船陸軍與數千名科林斯、克里特弓手構成的遮蔽方陣，戰後約三百艘安東尼戰船被奪或焚毀，俘虜以數千計。羅馬到亞克興的直線距離不足八百公里，埃及運來的穀船得靠這條線在數月內送到艦隊。圍城方面，公元前四十年的佩魯賈之圍歷時數月，跨過整個冬天。武器射程上，手拉式弩砲的有效射程約一百五十米，配重投石機可把石彈送出三百米以上，羅馬士兵的日糧約一公斤穀物、半公升酒與油。亞克興海戰後，屋大維在同年冬季取得埃及的實際控制權。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked sit at the two ends of the system, the unit and the ship. A Republican legion in this period numbered about five thousand four hundred to six thousand men in eighty centuries; after Caesar's reorganisation each legion also carried roughly one hundred and twenty archers, one hundred and twenty light skirmishers and three cavalry units of ten turmae, about thirty riders to a turma. Octavian raised eight legions on his own estates in 43 BC. The two battles of Philippi were fought a few days apart in October 42 BC, each side committing tens of thousands of men across a battlefield only a few miles deep; Brutus and Cassius killed themselves in December. The naval battles of Mylae and Naulochus in 36 BC decided the Sicilian theatre, and at Actium on 2 September 31 BC Antony put about five hundred ships into the line against roughly two hundred and sixty of Octavian's, the latter deeper in draught and heavier in the water, while Antony's ships carried the boarding infantry and the shielded phalanx of several thousand Cretan and Corinthian archers; afterwards about three hundred of Antony's ships were taken or burned, and the prisoners were counted in thousands. Rome lies less than eight hundred kilometres in a straight line from Actium, and the grain fleets from Egypt had to be brought down that line within a few months. The siege of Perugia in 40 BC lasted several months and ran through the whole winter. In weapon terms, the effective range of the cheiroballista was about one hundred and fifty metres, a torsion onager could throw its stone beyond three hundred metres, and a Roman soldier's daily ration was roughly a kilogram of grain with about half a litre of wine and oil. After Actium, Octavian took effective control of Egypt in the same winter.
cause: 根源在共和國權力分配的崩解。前二世紀中葉羅馬征服地中海之後，元老院與保民官之間的制衡被打破，擴張帶來的土地與財富集中到少數將軍手上。前六十年凱撒、龐培、克拉蘇結成第一次三頭同盟瓜分政府職位，三頭同盟在前五十三年克拉蘇戰死於卡雷之後裂解，龐培與元老院聯手對付凱撒，凱撒於前四十九年越過盧比孔河，開戰。前四十四年三月十五日部分元老刺殺凱撒，本意是終止獨裁，實際上卻沒有一方能約束散在各行省的邊疆軍團；凱撒遺囑把繼承權指定給年僅十六歲的屋大維，安東尼則掌握了執政官職位與羅馬本部的支持，兩人於前四十三年組成第二次三頭同盟清洗反對派。同一時間布魯圖斯與卡西烏斯拒絕承認新秩序，帶兵東去，於是原本的合法性競逐變成三個勢力爭奪同一批軍團與行省稅收的混戰。東方線上，馬其頓末代國王佩爾修斯求援於解放者、塞琉古系的殘餘勢力仍待收編、安東尼在埃及與帕提亞的婚姻與擴張野心，加上屋大維需要獨攬穀物與海運的航路控制，最後都變成了開戰的理由。
causeEn: The root of the matter was the breakdown of the distribution of power in the Republic. After Rome conquered the Mediterranean in the middle of the second century BC, the balance between Senate and tribunes of the plebs broke down, and the land and wealth that expansion brought were concentrated in the hands of a few generals. In the sixties BC Caesar, Pompey and Crassus formed the first triumvirate and divided the offices of government; when Crassus fell at Carrhae in 53 BC the triumvirate came apart, Pompey and the Senate combined against Caesar, and Caesar crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC and war began. When part of the Senate killed Caesar on 15 March 44 BC, the intention was to end the dictatorship, but no party was in a position to control the frontier legions scattered across the provinces; Caesar's will handed the succession to the sixteen-year-old Octavian, while Antony held the consulship and the support of Rome itself, and the two men formed the second triumvirate in 43 BC to purge the opposition. At the same time Brutus and Cassius refused to recognise the new order and marched east, so a contest over legitimacy turned into a struggle among three powers for the same legions and the same provincial tax revenue. On the eastern front, the last king of Macedon, Perseus, appealed to the Liberators, the surviving Seleucid interests still had to be absorbed, Antony's marriages and expansionist ambitions in Egypt and Parthia, and Octavian's need to control the grain and the shipping lanes all turned into reasons for going to war.
impact: 最深遠的影響是共和國的制度被清空。公元前四十二年腓立比之後解放者派覆亡，前三十六年內戰在西西里收場後，意大利境內再無成建制的反對派；第二次三頭同盟靠非常權力沒收財產、拆毀房屋，意大利城市的中產與元老階層在清洗與徵召中元氣盡傷，土地集中與退役老兵安置成為新秩序最迫切的問題，同時每個公民都明白國家的最高權力已落在軍隊手上。公元前三十一年亞克興之後，埃及被吞併，屋大維取得地中海東部的糧食與財富，公元前二十七年獲封奧古斯都，元老院、公民大會與選舉形式保留，實際統治集中於「第一公民」一人。長期看，這場內戰把羅馬從以公民軍團與元老院政治為基礎的共和國，改造成以常備邊疆軍隊為基礎的帝國；隨後兩個世紀的和平與擴張正運轉在這套軍事財政機器上，而軍隊與皇帝個人效忠的關係在此確立，日後的皇位繼承問題與禁衛軍政治都由此衍生。文化上，長期駐紮意大利的兵團把營區生活與拉丁口語帶進城市，希臘化東方的習慣隨俘虜與使節進入羅馬，而「凱撒」之名從此成為皇帝與專制權力的代名詞。
impactEn: The deepest effect was that the institutions of the Republic were hollowed out. After Philippi in 42 BC the Liberators were destroyed, and once the civil war closed in Sicily in 36 BC there was no organised opposition left inside Italy; the second triumvirate confiscated property and pulled down houses under extraordinary powers, the middle ranks and the senatorial order of the Italian cities were worn out by the purges and the levies, concentration of land and the settlement of discharged veterans became the most pressing problems of the new order, and every citizen understood that the highest power in the state now lay with the army. After Actium in 31 BC Egypt was swallowed up, and Octavian obtained the grain and the wealth of the eastern Mediterranean; in 27 BC he was acclaimed Augustus, and while the Senate, the assemblies and the elections kept their form, actual rule was concentrated in one man, the first citizen. In the long run the civil war turned Rome from a republic based on citizen legions and senatorial politics into an empire resting on permanent frontier armies; the two centuries of peace and expansion that followed ran on this military-fiscal machine, and the tie between the army and the personal loyalty of the emperor was fixed here, from which later questions of imperial succession and the politics of the Praetorian Guard derived. Culturally, the long presence of army camps in Italy carried barrack life and colloquial Latin into the towns, the habits of the Hellenistic east entered Rome with prisoners and envoys, and the name of Caesar became from that point on a synonym for the emperor and for autocratic power.

resultEn: At the Battle of Actium on 2 September 31 BC Octavian's fleet defeated Antony, who fell back with his remnants to Egypt, and in the following year Octavian followed him into Alexandria; in August 30 BC Antony and Cleopatra killed themselves in turn, the Ptolemaic dynasty came to an end, Egypt was turned into a Roman province, and its grain and ivory revenues went straight to Italy. Octavian now held the military, financial and priestly powers alone; in 27 BC he laid down the last of the triumvirate's offices and took the title Augustus, the old forms of Senate, consuls and popular assembly being kept in appearance while real power stayed in a single pair of hands. Looking back, the civil war that began in March 44 BC ran for fourteen years and passed through the stages of Philippi, Perugia, Mylae, Naulochus and Actium; the outcome was not that one side won entire and the other was wiped out, but that both were spent: Antony's party destroyed at sea, the Liberators annihilated as early as 42 BC, and the Senate never again an independent force. Rome now left the civil wars behind and entered a principate governed by one man, and nothing of the same scale would stir again until the fourth century AD.
